title: MB9-23321
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: On December 13, 2019, the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) of the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB or the Board) received an application to reopen the refugee claim of XXXX XXXX XXXX (the Applicant), a citizen of Democratic Republic of Congo, following an RPD decision made on October 31, 2019, concluding that the claim had been abandoned.

The RPD's jurisdiction to reopen a claim is limited since once the decision is made, the RPD becomes functus officio and could exercise its jurisdiction again only if a breach to a principle of natural justice is established.
On October 4, 2019, the claim of the Applicant was referred to the IRB.

On the same date, the Applicant was given a document entitled Confirmation of referral and Notice to Appear at the RPD, in which the Applicant was advised that she had 15 days to provide the Basis of Claim Form (BOC) and that, should she fail to provide the BOC within the 15-day deadline, a special hearing would be held on October 28, 2019 to explain why the BOC was not received by the RPD within the specified period.
A special hearing was held on October 28, 2019, at which the Applicant did not appear.
Although counsel is counsel of record since October 13, 2019, he too, did not appear on that date.
As a consequence of the Applicant's default to appear, the abandonment of her claim was pronounced on the same date, October 28,2019.
On October 30, 2019, the RPD forwarded to the Applicant, at the address of record, a Notice of Decision - Abandonment of a claim for refugee protection.
On November 4, 2019, the Applicant forwarded to the Board a Notification of Client Contact Information in which she advised the Board of her new address.
On November 25, 2019, the Board's letter containing the Notice of Decision - Abandonment of a claim for refugee protection was returned by the Post Office with the note "Moved/Uknown".
The Board forwarded the Notice of Decision to the new address of record on November 27, 2019.
As stated above, the Board received an application to reopen the claim of the Applicant on December 13, 2019.
In this application, counsel for the Applicant states that the BOC was "submitted with the timeframe it was expected to be file (sic) (2019-10-13) as appears on a copy of the fax attached".

The attachment to which counsel is referring is a Fax receipt dated December 12, 2019 at 20:49, addressed to the Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada stating "Veuillez trouver ci-joint une correspondance à porter à votre attention ", indicating that there are 26 pages.

The attachment also contains the BOCs of the Applicant and the minor child which would have been signed on October 13, 2019 but which bears a date stamp from the Board, two months later, that is, on December 13, 2019.
The Board processed the BOCs in its case management system, NOVA, on December 19, 2019.

It is not known why counsel states in his application that the BOCs would have been received by the Board on October 13, 2019 as there is no evidence of this fact, whether in the attachment provided by counsel or in the Board's record.
While the BOCs may have been signed on October 13, 2019, they were provided to the Board 2 months later, on December 13, 2019 as appears from the Board's date stamp.

The fax attachment to counsel's Application to reopen shows that the BOCs may have been forwarded to the Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada, on December 12, 2019 but it does not show that it was provided to the Board.

Moreover, while the Fax's receipt is dated December 12, 2020, the attachment (the BOCs) are stamped December 13, 2020, one day after the fax was sent, which means that they could not have been attached to the Fax receipt.
The tribunal then asked the Applicant to provide proof that the application to reopen this file be forwarded to the Minister in accordance with RPD Rule 62 (2).

On January 23, 2020, the Applicant provided the same document to which it is referred in paragraph 14 of the present decision, namely a Fax receipt dated December 12, 2019 at 20:49, addressed to the Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada stating "Veuillez trouver ci-joint une correspondance à porter à votre attention ", indicating that there are 26 pages.
The tribunal concludes that the Applicant did not comply with Rule 62 (2) and this action on his part could be interpreted as an attempt to mislead the Tribunal.
The tribunal finds that, in the circumstances of this case, a breach to a principle of natural justice has not been established.

After having considered the application of the Applicant and the circumstances as a whole, the tribunal determines that the Application to reopen the claim of the Applicant is denied.
